title: Present Simple Tense
description: Used for repeated actions, daily routines, general truths, and permanent situations. Add -s/-es for he/she/it.

title: Present Continuous Tense
description: Used for actions happening right now at the moment of speaking or temporary situations around now.

examples.sentence: They are watching a movie right now.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ ɑːr ˈwɒtʃɪŋ ə ˈmuːvi raɪt naʊ/

examples.sentence: I am living with my friends this week.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ æm ˈlɪvɪŋ wɪð maɪ frendz ðɪs wiːk/
examples.translation: Я живу у друзей на этой неделе.

title: Past Simple Tense
description: Used for completed actions in the past with a specific time mentioned (yesterday, last year, in 2010, ago).

examples.sentence: He bought a new car two days ago.
examples.phonetic: /hiː bɔːt ə njuː kɑːr tuː deɪz əˈɡoʊ/
examples.translation: Он купил новую машину два дня назад.

title: Present Perfect Tense
description: Connects the past with the present: focuses on life experience (ever/never), result now (already/yet/just), or unfinished time periods.

examples.sentence: I have already finished my homework.
examples.translation: Я уже сделал домашнее задание (результат налицо).

examples.sentence: Have you ever been to Japan?

title: First Conditional (Real Possibility)
description: Talks about real and possible situations in the future. Remember: do NOT use 'will' in the If-clause!

examples.sentence: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf ɪt reɪnz təˈmɒroʊ wiː wɪl steɪ æt hoʊm/
examples.translation: Если завтра пойдет дождь, мы останемся дома.

title: Articles: A, An, The
pattern: a/an + singular countable noun | the + specific noun
description: 'A/An' for non-specific singular countable items (first mention). 'The' when both speaker and listener know which specific item is meant.

examples.sentence: I saw a dog. The dog was barking.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ sɔː ə dɒɡ ðə dɒɡ wɒz ˈbɑːrkɪŋ/
examples.translation: Я увидел собаку (какую-то). Собака (эта конкретная) лаяла.
